set.descent_text: The route ends at the summit ridge, through a keyhole, and the walk-off from the summit is the descent. From the summit, head east about 20 feet from the west face, then south, downclimbing steep loose third class toward the anchors perched over the couloir cutting the south ridge. One single-rope rappel (a 60 m rope reaches) lands in the scree couloir, which you follow down, passing left through a narrow slot into the main couloir, to the base of the wall; then take the talus and scree back to camp. The gully is long and loose, so wear helmets and avoid knocking rocks onto the party below. Rappelling the Infinity Gauntlet line on short anchored rappels is an alternative.
set.approach: From the trailhead at Twin Lakes, follow the Robinson Creek trail west. No sign marks the turn into Little Slide Canyon, where the path forks between two large boulders. Cross Robinson Creek on a log or by wading, then pick a way through the boggy ground and side channels. A short steep stretch gains the canyon; keep left of the stream to a big talus field, cross over, and follow cairns through talus, trees and granite benches to the flat ground below the Hulk, west of the wall and under Maltby Lake. Many parties bivy there, though it can be done in a long day. The Red Dihedral starts at the right-hand end of the west face, close to the foot of the descent gully; third-class ledges lead left across the face to the foot of the climb.

review.notes: Standard descent and approach from the area page and a trip report; start from the route page.

set.descent_text: The route finishes on the left tip of the sharp summit ridge, which is not the true top. For the walk-off, traverse right roughly 100 to 150 yards, climb two moderate pitches shared with the Red Dihedral and pass through the manhole to the summit, then use the standard descent. From the summit, head east about 20 feet from the west face, then south, downclimbing steep loose third class toward the anchors perched over the couloir cutting the south ridge. One single-rope rappel (a 60 m rope reaches) lands in the scree couloir, which you follow down, passing left through a narrow slot into the main couloir, to the base of the wall; then take the talus and scree back to camp. The gully is long and loose, so wear helmets and avoid knocking rocks onto the party below. A quicker option from the ridge is to rappel the Venturi Effect, which has bolted anchors; a single 70 m rope works, and an 80 m rope skips some stations.

review.notes: Route page: ends at ridge tip, traverse and Venturi rappel; recess location from Tradewinds page.

set.descent_text: The Polish Route ends at the top of the formation. From there, either continue right to the summit and take the standard descent, or traverse back across ledges to rappel slings and drop into the gully; going off the back of the formation is also possible. For the standard descent: From the summit, head east about 20 feet from the west face, then south, downclimbing steep loose third class toward the anchors perched over the couloir cutting the south ridge. One single-rope rappel (a 60 m rope reaches) lands in the scree couloir, which you follow down, passing left through a narrow slot into the main couloir, to the base of the wall; then take the talus and scree back to camp. The gully is long and loose, so wear helmets and avoid knocking rocks onto the party below.

review.notes: Route page for the top-out and start; standard descent from the area page and trip report.

set.descent_text: Sunspot Dihedral finishes on the summit of the Hulk, so the standard descent applies. From the summit, head east about 20 feet from the west face, then south, downclimbing steep loose third class toward the anchors perched over the couloir cutting the south ridge. One single-rope rappel (a 60 m rope reaches) lands in the scree couloir, which you follow down, passing left through a narrow slot into the main couloir, to the base of the wall; then take the talus and scree back to camp. The gully is long and loose, so wear helmets and avoid knocking rocks onto the party below. If weather turns, the Venturi Effect rappels, about 20 feet south of the Positive Vibrations top-out, are a bolted escape with a 70 m rope, though slow.
set.approach: From the trailhead at Twin Lakes, follow the Robinson Creek trail west. No sign marks the turn into Little Slide Canyon, where the path forks between two large boulders. Many parties bivy there, though it can be done in a long day. The route shares its start with Positive Vibrations, a blocky dihedral on the left side of a prominent triangle in the lower face, so expect a queue.

review.notes: Route page: summit finish, start and Venturi escape.

set.descent_text: Astrohulk ends at the Recliner ledge; from there climb cracks on the right to the ridgeline, or traverse left on fourth class to the Venturi Effect and rappel it with a 70 m rope. From the ridge, reach the summit and use the standard descent: class 3 east then south to a chute, one single-rope rappel, then down the south-west couloir. Take care in the long, loose gully.
set.approach: From the trailhead at Twin Lakes, follow the Robinson Creek trail west. No sign marks the turn into Little Slide Canyon, where the path forks between two large boulders. Many parties bivy there, though it can be done in a long day. Astrohulk follows the first four pitches of Positive Vibrations, so go to the Positive Vibrations start on the face.

review.notes: Route page: Recliner ledge, ridge and Venturi options; shares start with Positive Vibrations.

set.descent_text: Airstream reaches the summit ridge. Reach the true summit by following the Red Dihedral's upper pitches, then take the standard descent: class 3 east then south to a chute, one single-rope rappel, then down the south-west couloir. The alternative from the ridge is to rappel the Venturi Effect. The scree gully is loose, so move carefully.
set.approach: From the trailhead at Twin Lakes, follow the Robinson Creek trail west. No sign marks the turn into Little Slide Canyon, where the path forks between two large boulders. Many parties bivy there, though it can be done in a long day. Airstream starts in the crack system just right of the Polish Route's first-pitch corner, between the Polish Route and Positive Vibrations; it shares this start with Solar Flare.

review.notes: Route pages: ridge finish, Venturi rappel, start between Polish and Positive Vibrations.

set.descent_text: The Venturi Effect finishes on the ridgeline. From there you can carry on along the ridge to the summit by way of the last two Red Dihedral pitches and take the standard descent: class 3 east then south to a chute, one single-rope rappel, then down the south-west couloir. Or rappel the route's bolted stations with a 70 m rope; this line is also the usual bail for neighbouring climbs. The gully route is loose.
set.approach: From the trailhead at Twin Lakes, follow the Robinson Creek trail west. No sign marks the turn into Little Slide Canyon, where the path forks between two large boulders. A short steep stretch gains the canyon; keep left of the stream to a big talus field, cross over, and follow cairns through talus, trees and granite benches to the flat ground below the Hulk, west of the wall and under Maltby Lake. Many parties bivy there, though it can be done in a long day. The Venturi Effect starts on a thin flake just left of the wide crack of Eye of the Storm, up a short scramble to a large pedestal.

review.notes: Route page: ridge finish and rappel; start shared with Eye of the Storm.

set.descent_text: Tradewinds ends at the Crow's Nest ledge. From there, finish by the splitter on the Venturi Effect or traverse right onto Astrohulk, or simply rappel with a 70 m rope. At the ridge, the walk-off is class 3 east then south to a chute, one single-rope rappel, then down the south-west couloir.
set.approach: From the trailhead at Twin Lakes, follow the Robinson Creek trail west. No sign marks the turn into Little Slide Canyon, where the path forks between two large boulders. Tradewinds begins in a clean corner roughly 40 feet right of the triangular recess, the left edge of which is where Positive Vibrations starts.

review.notes: Route page: ledge finish, options, rope length.

set.descent_text: Infinity Gauntlet finishes on the summit, via a flared splitter. Descend by rappelling the route on bolted anchors; no rappel is longer than 35 m, so the descent suits a single rope. The same rappel line serves the Red Dihedral and Eye of the Storm. This is easier than the standard descent of scrambling, one rappel and a long loose gully. Rockfall is a concern, so keep clear of the junky dihedrals right of the route.
set.approach: From the trailhead at Twin Lakes, follow the Robinson Creek trail west. No sign marks the turn into Little Slide Canyon, where the path forks between two large boulders. A short steep stretch gains the canyon; keep left of the stream to a big talus field, cross over, and follow cairns through talus, trees and granite benches to the flat ground below the Hulk, west of the wall and under Maltby Lake. Many parties bivy there, though it can be done in a long day. The route starts about 100 feet left of the Red Dihedral on a wide right-leaning ramp, roughly 100 feet right of Tradewinds.

review.notes: Route page and AAJ article agree on rappels of 35 m or less back to the ground and the start.

set.descent_text: Choose Joy tops out on the ridge where it joins the final pitch of Eye of the Storm. The usual descent is to rappel the route with one 80 m rope, using the anchors at the belays and stopping at each station. Knot the rope ends. Lower down, the line passes the Astrohulk, Lenticular and Tradewinds stations.
set.approach: From the trailhead at Twin Lakes, follow the Robinson Creek trail west. No sign marks the turn into Little Slide Canyon, where the path forks between two large boulders. Cross Robinson Creek on a log or by wading, then pick a way through the boggy ground and side channels. A short steep stretch gains the canyon; keep left of the stream to a big talus field, cross over, and follow cairns through talus, trees and granite benches to the flat ground below the Hulk, west of the wall and under Maltby Lake. Many parties bivy there, though it can be done in a long day. Choose Joy starts at the lowest middle point of the Hulk, right of and below the shared start of the Venturi Effect, Eye of the Storm and Lenticular, about 30 feet left of Tradewinds. Look for a separate dihedral with four bolts about 20 feet up.

review.notes: Route page; AAJ report of the route as second source for existence.

set.descent_text: Lenticular Gyrations ends at the top belay with no summit. The easiest way down is the Venturi Effect rappels with a single 70 m rope; two 60 m ropes also let you rappel most of the route itself. To escape from lower on the route, walk left along the Bivy Ledge to the Venturi rappel station.
set.approach: From the trailhead at Twin Lakes, follow the Robinson Creek trail west. No sign marks the turn into Little Slide Canyon, where the path forks between two large boulders. Lenticular Gyrations shares its start with Eye of the Storm: scramble up past the Venturi Effect start to a large pedestal, and begin in the big corner on top of it.

review.notes: Route page and Venturi page agree on the 70 m Venturi rappel.

set.descent_text: Eye of the Storm tops out on the ridge. A common way down is to skip the final pitch and rappel the Venturi Effect stations; the Infinity Gauntlet rappel line also serves it. Otherwise continue to the summit for the standard descent.

review.notes: Route page; Infinity Gauntlet page names it on the shared rappel line.

set.descent_text: Lost in the Sun does not reach the summit; descend by rappelling the route, with an 80 m rope or two ropes (a 70 m rope plus a short pull line also works). Skip the second-pitch anchor, which sits off to the side. Another option is a short climb up and left from the last belay to join the Red Dihedral.
set.approach: From the trailhead at Twin Lakes, follow the Robinson Creek trail west. No sign marks the turn into Little Slide Canyon, where the path forks between two large boulders. review.notes: Route page only for route specifics.

set.descent_text: Solar Flare ends at the top of the Sunspot. From the last belay you can climb right to join the Sunspot Dihedral to the ridge and summit, or rappel. Rappel with a 70 m rope, knotting the ends; skip the sixth-pitch anchor. Lower down, rappels lead to the Polish Route and Blowhard anchors, and from there a 70 m rappel reaches the gully.
set.approach: From the trailhead at Twin Lakes, follow the Robinson Creek trail west. No sign marks the turn into Little Slide Canyon, where the path forks between two large boulders. Cross Robinson Creek on a log or by wading, then pick a way through the boggy ground and side channels. A short steep stretch gains the canyon; keep left of the stream to a big talus field, cross over, and follow cairns through talus, trees and granite benches to the flat ground below the Hulk, west of the wall and under Maltby Lake. review.notes: Route page and Airstream page agree on the shared start.

set.descent_text: Blowhard ends at the top of the Polish Tower. All anchors are bolted for rappel, and an 80 m rope is recommended. Descend the route this way, or continue along the ridge above to the summit for the standard descent.
set.approach: From the trailhead at Twin Lakes, follow the Robinson Creek trail west. No sign marks the turn into Little Slide Canyon, where the path forks between two large boulders. Cross Robinson Creek on a log or by wading, then pick a way through the boggy ground and side channels. A short steep stretch gains the canyon; keep left of the stream to a big talus field, cross over, and follow cairns through talus, trees and granite benches to the flat ground below the Hulk, west of the wall and under Maltby Lake. Many parties bivy there, though it can be done in a long day. Blowhard starts up a right-facing corner just left of the Polish Route.

review.notes: Route page and Escape from Poland page agree on an 80 m rappel of Blowhard.

set.descent_text: This variation finishes on the ridge. From there, descend roughly 60 feet on foot to the summit of the Polish Tower and rappel Blowhard with an 80 m rope; alternatively, climb to the top of the Sunspot and rappel with an 80 m rope, or continue to the summit.
set.approach: From the trailhead at Twin Lakes, follow the Robinson Creek trail west. No sign marks the turn into Little Slide Canyon, where the path forks between two large boulders. Cross Robinson Creek on a log or by wading, then pick a way through the boggy ground and side channels. A short steep stretch gains the canyon; keep left of the stream to a big talus field, cross over, and follow cairns through talus, trees and granite benches to the flat ground below the Hulk, west of the wall and under Maltby Lake. Many parties bivy there, though it can be done in a long day. Escape from Poland branches from the Polish Route: climb the Polish Route to the bolted anchor atop its offwidth, shared with Blowhard.

set.descent_text: Green Thunder ends on the summit of the Polish Tower. You can rappel the route with an 80 m rope but need directionals; the easier way is to rappel Blowhard to its second belay ledge, keeping on its right face so you are not swung onto the overhanging wall, then finish on the talus beneath the north side of the Hulk.
set.approach: From the trailhead at Twin Lakes, follow the Robinson Creek trail west. No sign marks the turn into Little Slide Canyon, where the path forks between two large boulders. Cross Robinson Creek on a log or by wading, then pick a way through the boggy ground and side channels. A short steep stretch gains the canyon; keep left of the stream to a big talus field, cross over, and follow cairns through talus, trees and granite benches to the flat ground below the Hulk, west of the wall and under Maltby Lake. Many parties bivy there, though it can be done in a long day. The north side is shady. Green Thunder starts about 300 feet up and left of Blowhard, under a huge overhanging left-facing corner with a wide crack; scramble about 100 feet of third class to a belay below three bolts.

review.notes: Route page and Up in Smoke page agree on the start and a rappel with an 80 m rope.

set.descent_text: Up in Smoke ends at a belay on the far left side of the Polish Tower. Anchors are bolted and the route rappels easily with an 80 m rope; a 70 m rope probably works.
set.approach: From the trailhead at Twin Lakes, follow the Robinson Creek trail west. No sign marks the turn into Little Slide Canyon, where the path forks between two large boulders. Cross Robinson Creek on a log or by wading, then pick a way through the boggy ground and side channels. A short steep stretch gains the canyon; keep left of the stream to a big talus field, cross over, and follow cairns through talus, trees and granite benches to the flat ground below the Hulk, west of the wall and under Maltby Lake. Many parties bivy there, though it can be done in a long day. Up in Smoke is the leftmost line on the shady north face. Hike up past Blowhard to the overhanging corner that starts Green Thunder, scramble third-class ledges to the Green Thunder start ledge, and start about 25 feet left in a dirty right-facing corner.

review.notes: Route page and Green Thunder page agree on start ledge.

set.descent_text: Beeline tops out on the summit; a large cairn near the top on the right marks the way to the rappel station of the standard descent. From the summit, head east about 20 feet from the west face, then south, downclimbing steep loose third class toward the anchors perched over the couloir cutting the south ridge. One single-rope rappel (a 60 m rope reaches) lands in the scree couloir, which you follow down, passing left through a narrow slot into the main couloir, to the base of the wall; then take the talus and scree back to camp. The gully is long and loose, so wear helmets and avoid knocking rocks onto the party below. Rock gets worse near the top, with many loose blocks.
set.approach: From the trailhead at Twin Lakes, follow the Robinson Creek trail west. No sign marks the turn into Little Slide Canyon, where the path forks between two large boulders. Cross Robinson Creek on a log or by wading, then pick a way through the boggy ground and side channels. A short steep stretch gains the canyon; keep left of the stream to a big talus field, cross over, and follow cairns through talus, trees and granite benches to the flat ground below the Hulk, west of the wall and under Maltby Lake. Many parties bivy there, though it can be done in a long day. Beeline is on the far right side of the Hulk: walk uphill from the Red Dihedral start, past the Falling Dihedral, to a big red wall with three cracks.

review.notes: Route page: summit finish, cairn, start.
